chunks: A man congratulated another man who had been given a son, and said: “May the horseman bring you joy.” Al-Hasan ibn Ali عليه السلام said to him: “How do you know that he will be a horseman or a footman?” He said to him: “May I be made your ransom, then what should I say?” He said: “Say: You have thanked the Giver, and may there be blessing for you in the one gifted, and may he reach his full strength, and may you be granted his righteousness.”

key_terms.الْمَوْهُوبِ: the gifted one, referring to the child bestowed
key_terms.الْوَاهِبَ: the Giver, meaning Allah who grants children

ai.seo_question: What should be said when congratulating someone on the birth of a son in Islamic etiquette?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the proper etiquette of congratulating someone on the birth of a child. Rather than making uncertain assumptions about the child’s future, one should offer a supplication centered on gratitude to Allah, blessing for the child, maturity, and righteousness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4687 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

A man congratulated another man on the birth of a son by saying, "May this young warrior bring you joy!"
Imam Hasan ibn Ali (as)said to him: "How do you know whether he will be a warrior or one who walks on foot?"
The man replied: "May I be sacrificed for you! What should I say then?"
Imam (as) said: "Say: May you thank the Giver, may the gift be blessed for you, may he reach maturity, and may you be granted his righteousness."
